Subject: Hosted API questionnaire — data residency + retention

Hi Rishi —

Thanks for taking this. As part of our procurement/security review we have a short set of clarifying questions about Redwood's Hosted API handling of customer data (residency, retention, deletion). We're trying to confirm that AurAnova's PII and conversational logs stay within the US and can be fully deleted on request. Specific asks below — can you respond with short, auditable answers and any evidence (flow diagrams, retention matrix)?

1) Where is customer request data stored at rest by default (region/locations)? Any cross-region replication?
2) Default retention windows for request payloads, generated completions, logs/traces, and cached KV/prefix cache. Can customers change these?
3) Deletion process: what happens when a customer requests account-level erasure? Timeline for removal from serving, backups, and audit logs.
4) Do backup snapshots remain after logical deletion and if so, for how long? Are backups encrypted and where?
5) Any circumstances where data would leave the US for processing (e.g., third-party analytics, model training)?
6) Where are audit logs stored and how long are they retained?

We'd like answers by EOD Wed (Dec 6) if possible. Attached is our template security questionnaire — I populated the header.

Thanks,
Aliza
Aliza Khan
Security Program Manager, AurAnova

Team — forwarding AurAnova's questionnaire. They want auditable answers + a data flow diagram and retention matrix. Sergio / Neha, can you confirm the precise numbers below and whether we have any customer-specific config switches to offer? Laura — please hold this for the ANV deal record (ANV-2028-209).

Draft answers (please review/edit):
- Default at-rest storage: customer request artifacts (payloads, completions) are stored in US regions by default (primary: us-west-2). Cross-region replication is disabled for hosted accounts unless explicitly requested; we do not replicate customer data to EU/APAC for standard hosted customers.
- Retention defaults: request metadata & text: 30 days; telemetry traces/errors: 90 days; cached prefix/KV entries: 48 hours default (configurable per account up to 7 days); embeddings/derived artifacts: 90 days (when used). Customers can request custom retention windows on contract for Dedicated/Private; hosted customers can request adjustments via support but longer/shorter windows may require contractual terms.
- Deletion workflow: on account erasure request we mark data for immediate logical deletion (soft-delete) and remove access from the serving layer within 2 hours. Background jobs perform physical deletion from object stores and index stores within a 30-day window; backup snapshots are subject to snapshot lifecycle (see below).
- Backups: encrypted S3 snapshots (server-side AES-256) are retained for 90 days by default; snapshots are immutable during retention window. Customers may request expedited purging of snapshots as part of a data transfer/erasure contract; this requires execution of our backup-rewrite workflow and takes up to 30 additional days.
- Cross-region/process exceptions: we do not use customer request content to train models. Analytics/aggregate metrics are non-identifying and processed in US-only controls; third-party integrators are vetted and must have equivalent controls.
- Audit logs: security audit logs retained 365 days; operational request traces retained 90 days.

Attachments we should prepare: redwood-data-flow-diagram.pdf, hostedapi-retention-matrix-auranova.xlsx.

Please correct any inaccuracies. Sergio — can you confirm encryption/KMS wording (customer-managed keys availability on Dedicated/Private)?

Thanks,
Rishi

Rishi —

Thanks for the quick draft. A few clarifications before we share with our InfoSec board: 
- Backups: when you say snapshots are "immutable" for 90 days, does that mean they cannot be deleted earlier even if a customer requests erasure? If so, do you provide attestations that snapshots were purged after lifecycle expiration?
- Deletion timeline: removing from serving in 2 hours is good — can you confirm the 30-day physical deletion is the maximum time or a target? Our compliance requires maximum 60 days from request for hosted vendors.
- KMS/keys: does hosted API support customer-provided keys (BYOK) or only Redwood-managed keys? If only Redwood-managed, is the key material ever exported or shared with third parties?
- Cross-region: please explicitly confirm whether any telemetry or error traces are sent to non-US regions for crash analysis.

If you can provide those clarifications and the diagram/matrix we'll route to legal.

Best,

Hi Aliza —

Thanks — please find concise, auditable answers below and two attachments (data flow diagram + retention matrix). If you want a signed attestation we can arrange one via our compliance team (SLA/addendum).

1) Region / replication
- Default storage: US primary region us-west-2. No automatic cross-region replication for standard Hosted API accounts. Cross-region replication is only enabled on a per-customer basis via contractual agreement.

2) Retention defaults (hosted API)
- Request payloads and generated completions: retained 30 days by default.
- Operational traces & telemetry (errors, performance traces): retained 90 days.
- In-memory/KV/prefix cache: default TTL 48 hours; configurable up to 7 days on hosted accounts by request; Dedicated/Private customers have full config control.
- Derived artifacts (embeddings, rerank indexes): retained 90 days by default unless customer explicitly persists them longer.
- Customers may request shorter retention; we will consider and implement via support/contract for hosted accounts.

3) Deletion process & timelines
- Step 1 (immediate): upon customer erasure request we mark account data as soft-deleted and revoke access to all serving lanes within ~2 hours.
- Step 2 (background): a reclamation job queues physical deletion of objects and indices. For hosted accounts the target window for physical deletion is 30 days; the maximum window we guarantee for hosted accounts is 60 days from request.
- Step 3 (backups): snapshots created for operational continuity are immutable for their configured retention window. Default snapshot retention is 90 days; snapshots that contain customer data will not be proactively mutated, but we support an expedited purge workflow (backup-rewrite) that we execute on a per-contract basis — expedited purges can take up to an additional 30 days depending on snapshot distribution.

4) Backups & attestations
- Backups are encrypted at rest (AES-256) in S3 buckets under our US account and are not exported to external regions by default.
- We maintain deletion and retention audit trails; upon request we can provide an attestation of purge once the expedited purge job completes. For formal attestations or contractual retention reductions we typically use a written addendum (we're happy to sign).

5) Keys & KMS
- Hosted API: Redwood-managed KMS keys by default (AWS KMS with customer partitioning). We do not export key material to third parties.
- Customer-provided keys (BYOK) are available for Dedicated/Private customers; for hosted customers we can discuss a managed-key model with per-tenant key separation under contract.

6) Cross-region processing / telemetry
- We do not send raw customer request content outside the configured US region for hosted customers. Aggregate telemetry and anonymized metrics used for system health stay in the US by default; we do not route identifiable traces to non-US processors. Any third-party observability exporters are vetted and documented in the attestation.

7) Audit logs
- Security/audit logs retention: 365 days by default. Operational request traces: 90 days. Access to audit logs is controlled via RBAC and logged.

Attachments included: redwood-data-flow-diagram.pdf (high-level components + where data resides), hostedapi-retention-matrix-auranova.xlsx (per-artifact retention and purge paths).

If you'd like, we can prepare a short 20-minute call with our Compliance team to review the attestation language and backup-rewrite workflow.

Thanks — happy to tighten language for your legal team.
